reason: Not computed (argument only). Weil descent of S_3 uses the F_2 field representation, so the CGK generic bound does not apply here. But a branching order is not new mathematics: it only changes how the solver searches the same CNF-XOR. Upper bound: for S_3(x1,x2,xR) with x1,x2 in an l-dim F_2-subspace V, fixing the l basis coefficients of x1 leaves a quadratic in x2 that Gauss-Jordan plus at most one extra branch handles. So the l coefficients of x1 are a strong backdoor of size l, and any reasonable order already costs <= 2^l * poly. Lower bound (heuristic): the system has about 2^{2l-n} solutions, and the search must cover the 2^l choices of x1 unless the solver finds a lower-degree certificate. Default CMS on descended S_3 already measures about 1 bit per l (programme measurement: d_ff=2, d_F<=k+2). So slope in l is pinned near 1 from above by the backdoor and from below by enumeration. A drop of 0.2 would need a sub-l backdoor, which means a degree drop in the descended ideal: the open d_F lever (§2), not a branching heuristic. The relation probability 2^{2l-n} is unchanged. Any learned-order gain is engineering or a constant factor unless it shows up as a backdoor of size < l.

Only a backdoor of size < l at n=23 would count as an advance, and it would reduce to a d_F statement.
